structural: The only structural obligation in the text is the prescribed signature: the quoted clause `fn fingerprint(&self) -> Fingerprint;` on `trust_but_verify::domain::NodeContents`. A version that took `&mut self`, returned a different type, or lived on another trait could still produce the same fingerprints. It would not match the declared interface, so this clause is not discretionary.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[NodeContents]/fn[fingerprint]` declares exactly `fn fingerprint(&self) -> Fingerprint;` and is marked `{impl}` for this requirement. The `Send + Sync` supertrait bound shown in the snippet is on `trait[NodeContents]`. That trait carries its own `{impl}` marker for `requirements.sdk.graph.NodeContents`, so I treated the bound as part of that declaration and not as an obligation of this requirement.

The remaining clauses only describe observable behavior of implementations:
- describing the contents "without further resource reads or querying mutable external state";
- "the same contents under the same rules give the same fingerprint";
- retaining the rules and their version, and changing the scheme when the rules change.

An implementation can satisfy these in many ways, and the text names no library, algorithm or type for them. They are verified by tests of concrete `NodeContents` implementations, not by structural evidence here.

The cited `requirements.sdk.graph.node_content` (the `Domain::node_content` signature) is context only. The `{term}` definitions are vocabulary and add no structural obligations. The review root is the only implementation root needed, and no acknowledgments apply.

behavioral: **Obligations**
1. `fingerprint` describes the retained contents. It makes no further resource reads and does not query mutable external state.
2. The same contents under the same rules give the same fingerprint.
3. The fingerprint retains the rules and their version, so changed rules give a changed scheme. Scheme and digest both take part in comparison, per `requirements.sdk.graph.observation_fingerprint`.

**Coverage**
- **No further reads or mutable state.**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot]` reads a snapshot, then changes the underlying graph contents from "before" to "after". It asserts that `snapshot.content.fingerprint()` still equals `snapshot.fingerprint`, that the value is still "before", and that the read log is still `[1]`. A fingerprint that re-read the graph would fail these assertions.
  - `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirement_edges_and_input_freshness_use_the_sdk]` repeats the check for the real Habeas domain. It rewrites `src/lib.rs` after reading retained contents. It then asserts that the retained reference-set fingerprint and the retained source fingerprint are unchanged. It also asserts that freshly read contents give a different fingerprint.
- **Same contents, same fingerprint.** In the same sdk test, the fingerprint of an input read through `ctx.read` equals the fingerprint of a separate `domain.node_content` read of the same selector. In the contracts test, repeated calls on the retained content equal the stored fingerprint.
- **Scheme and rules.** The sdk test asserts exact `Fingerprint` values for the reference set (scheme `habeas-reference-set-v1`) and for the input (scheme `habeas-input-v1`, with a pinned digest). Changing either the rules or the scheme would fail these assertions. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[wildcard_versions_still_check_inputs_and_errors]` shows that the scheme participates in comparison: a dependency with a different scheme and the same value is not current.

**Scope notes**
- The outline-content fingerprint rules belong to the refining `requirements.sdk.outlines.*` requirements. Those requirements carry their own review, so they are not reassessed here.
- Whether a developer changes the scheme when the rules change is a development convention. The pinned scheme and digest assertions are the available regression check for it.

I found no unexercised observable obligation and no marking gap.
